2608.03874.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
2608.03874.paper_summary: Modern agent frameworks equip large language models with external skill libraries to solve complex tasks. However, it remains unclear whether these systems can effectively evolve their skills and whether the resulting skills improve task-solving capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning. It covers five representative domains, each containing 100 interconnected subtasks ordered by increasing difficulty and opportunities for cross-task skill reuse. Our experiments show that sequential execution generally improves performance, but the gains vary substantially across models and domains. Moreover, in-context learning performs comparably to explicit skill maintenance on average, suggesting that much of the improvement arises from adaptation to prior context and feedback rather than reusable skill abstraction alone. Explicit skills nevertheless provide selective benefits for tasks requiring reusable procedures or precise outputs. We further find that less capable models tend to accumulate larger, more fragmented collections of task-specific skills. These findings show that current in-context skill evolution mechanisms can support continual adaptation, but still struggle to consistently consolidate experience into robust and transferable skills.
2608.03874.paper_summary_zh: 現代代理框架為大型語言模型配備外部技能庫，以解決複雜任務。然而，這些系統是否能有效地進化其技能，以及所產生的技能是否能改善任務解決能力，仍然不清楚。為了彌補這一差距，我們引入了ContinualSkillBench，一個動態評估框架，用於上下文中的持續技能學習。它涵蓋五個具有代表性的領域，每個領域包含100個相互關聯的子任務，按難度逐漸增加並提供跨任務技能重用的機會。我們的實驗顯示，順序執行通常能提高性能，但增益在模型和領域之間差異顯著。此外，平均而言，上下文學習的表現與明確的技能維護相當，這表明大部分改進來自於對先前上下文和反饋的適應，而非僅僅是可重用的技能抽象。然而，明確的技能仍然為需要可重用程序或精確輸出的任務提供選擇性好處。我們進一步發現，能力較弱的模型往往會累積更大且更零散的任務特定技能集合。這些發現顯示，當前的上下文技能進化機制可以支持持續適應，但仍然難以將經驗穩定地整合為穩健且可轉移的技能。
